claims.text: All three artifacts describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-00111 and the 07:47:40 start appear on the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger — so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the governing distance the trip ran 29.98 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km or 24.92%, which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%). The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence and the rider has discharged her initial burden.

The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 29.98 km, not the trip record's rounded 30.0 km; the trace figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes the threshold test run on, and it is the trace's 229 fixes at 10 second intervals with 100% coverage and no gaps that carry the excess of 5.98 km. The rider asks that the establishment test be run on that field and not on the convenience copy.

The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: no upfront quote was fixed at booking, and POL-RD-02 is therefore the operative remedy on this trip rather than a pass-through-only correction.

No exculpatory route other than the closure is open to the driver: the booked optimum of 24.0 km stands because the trip record carries no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no re-quote exists; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute a matched-itinerary baseline and solo_optimal_distance_km is irrelevant here.

The chat log records no instruction from the rider. Her only message, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver: with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test cannot be run at all, and a reply fixing a time of arrival cannot be converted into a rider-requested detour that would exonerate the excess.

The driver's only route to exculpation is POL-RD-03, and that exoneration is capped: the justified excess is the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00, computed from the advisory's own shortest_lawful_alternative_km on the record, and any distance beyond that cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal. The rider asks the judge to run that cap on this record's figures rather than treating the existence of the advisory as excusing the whole of the trip, and to refund whatever the cap does not cover.

On the rider's primary case, that the closure does not account for the whole of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the ruling to state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines: recomputed on the booked optimum, ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 31.00 against a charged_total of 37.74, an overcharge of 6.74; the payable figure is then rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor applies.

The rider's profile does not engage the extra corroboration rule in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4 that the clause sets (and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, which only matters once the count reaches 4), so her claim of 24.92% excess is subject to the ordinary burden and needs no corroboration beyond the trace.

claims.text: The booked optimal route runs BKE southbound then PIE westbound, and the LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, from 07:10 to 09:30 on the morning of the trip. That is the exact expressway segment the optimal route traverses, it is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE, its geometry intersects the route (intersects_route true) and its validity window brackets the entire trip (overlaps_trip_window true). The first limb of POL-RD-03 is therefore satisfied on the face of the advisory, not on the driver's say-so.

The second and third limbs of POL-RD-03 are met too. The advisory directs a diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd, and the driver's route was Upper Bukit Timah then the AYE - the route leaves the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoins it further on. The trace is clean corroboration of a deliberate diversion rather than a wander: 229 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, with speeds varying by road class (0.0 / 20.6 / 46.5 / 71.0 kph) as an expressway-then-arterial-then-expressway route would. The advisory's shortest_lawful_alternative_km of 29.2 km sits almost exactly on the trace's 29.98 km.

The exoneration cap in POL-RD-03 is not reached, so the whole excess is excused. The cap is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The justified excess is therefore the entire measured excess, the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, and no excess survives for POL-RD-02 to refund. Note the governing distance figure is the trace's 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires.

Even if the tribunal declined to exonerate in full, the arithmetic still lands on NO_ACTION. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route - 29.98 km at a duration of 30.0 x (29.98 / 24.0) = 37.5 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585, against a charged_total of SGD 37.74. The difference is roughly SGD 0.16, far below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so POL-RD-02 produces NO_ACTION in any event. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

The deviation is established but is nowhere near MATERIAL. The excess of 5.98 km is 24.92% of the 24.0 km optimal: it clears the establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but falls well short of the materiality gate of 50% or 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile inquiry is not triggered at all. For completeness, were it triggered it would find nothing: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, so no pattern under POL-RD-06 exists. This is an ordinary unavoidable detour, not a material one.

The driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 places on him by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general complaint that traffic was bad. Traffic advisory ADV-20260803-014, a third-party LTA_DATAMALL closure of the very segment the optimal route uses, is invoked under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the discharge the clause demands of the driver once the rider has shown excess.

The chat log shows the diversion was announced in advance and not contested. At 07:54:20 the driver messaged the rider in-app that the PIE towards Tuas was closed by a lorry fire and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang; the rider read the message at 07:54:48 and replied at 07:54:55 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. The driver's contemporaneous account matches the LTA advisory and the trace, which is why his account of the closure should be preferred over the rider's later recollection.

There is no ERP or toll pass-through correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09. The fare breakdown carries tolls_erp of 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the optimal route crosses no gantry at this hour (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Even on the rider's best case, the standalone pass-through limb of POL-RD-09(2) has nothing to settle and adds nothing to the claim.

The rider's assertion 'I did not see any closure' cites no artifact and is contradicted by a timestamped government advisory covering the disputed segment. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded; it cannot outweigh ADV-20260803-014, which was active from 07:10 and covered the whole trip window. The rider's own profile is context only and she meets none of the gateways that would let any profile field stand in for evidence about this trip.

ruling.explanation: Both parties: the trip did deviate from the booked optimal route. The GPS trace shows 29.98 km against a 24.0 km optimal, an excess of 5.98 km or 24.92%, which clears POL-RD-01's establishment tests. However, the deviation is fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. The LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 confirms a HIGH-severity closure of the PIE towards Tuas after Clementi Rd, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, active 07:10 to 09:30 and overlapping the whole trip window. That is the segment the booked optimal route uses. The GPS trace shows the driver left the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoined via Upper Bukit Timah and the AYE, matching the advisory's diversion. POL-RD-03 caps exoneration at min(measured excess, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km, so the entire measured excess is justified. No excess remains for POL-RD-02. Even if the fare were recomputed against the closure-adjusted optimal route (29.98 km and 37.5 minutes), the difference from the charged total would be about SGD 0.16, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. There is no ERP or toll correction: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty. The rider's statement that she saw no closure is noted, but it cites no artifact and is outweighed by the timestamped government advisory and the driver's contemporaneous in-app message. The deviation is not material (24.92% is below 50%, and 5.98 km is below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile inquiry and any conduct referral are not triggered. The evidence artifacts relied on all carry full weight 1.0. The charge stands and no refund is due.

To both parties: the charge stands, and no refund or compensation is due.

Distance and deviation. The trip from Blk 511 Woodlands Dr 14 to Fusionopolis ran 29.98 km on the GPS trace (the governing figure under POL-RD-01, not the trip record's rounded 30.0 km) against a booked optimal of 24.0 km. That is an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.92% — it passes both establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is established. It does not reach materiality: the materiality gate is more than 50% or more than 8.0 km, and 24.92% / 5.98 km falls well short. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, so no driver-conduct referral arises. (In any case driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern exists.)

Why the deviation is excused. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260803-014 (EV-ADVIS-00111-01, weight 1.0) records a HIGH-severity closure of the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, active 07:10–09:30, on the very segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses, with its geometry intersecting that route and its window bracketing the whole trip. The trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining via the AYE, exactly the diversion the advisory directs. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met.

The rider asked the tribunal to apply the POL-RD-03 cap rather than treat the advisory as excusing the whole trip. That is the correct test and it has been applied. The justified excess is min(measured 5.98 km, 1.30 × (29.2 − 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The cap (7.76 km) exceeds the measured excess, so the whole of the 5.98 km is excused and no excess survives for POL-RD-02 to refund.

Even if it did, the arithmetic would not move money. Run against the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration ~37.5 min), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 × 29.98 + 0.28 × 37.5) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact carrying it) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.58, against a charged total of SGD 37.74 — roughly SGD 0.16, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 (upfront pricing) does not apply. Charged total 37.74; recomputed fare 37.58; refund 0.16, de minimis.

Pass-through and billing lines. POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, no airport surcharge applies (the trip does not originate at an airport), and no gantry or surcharge line appears that the trace never crosses. There is no pass-through correction to add on top of the exoneration and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding. POL-RD-05 does not run (no pickup or dropoff amendment; amended_optimal_distance_km null) and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_X, not a pooled trip). POL-RD-04 does not exonerate anything: the rider's only chat message named no road and carries no waypoint_hint.

Burden and integrity. The rider discharged her initial burden under POL-RD-08 (matching trip IDs TRP-00111, matching 07:47:40 start, excess over threshold), and the driver discharged his in turn by pointing to a specific artifact and clause: LTA advisory ADV-20260803-014 invoked under POL-RD-03. His in-app message at 07:54:20 announcing the closure, and the rider's reply, are consistent with that account. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 100% coverage, 229 fixes at 10 s intervals, no gaps, 0 s maximum gap — so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not engage. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. Confidence rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0, and the admissibility weights cap confidence at 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your fare stands. To the driver: the diversion is excused.

Same trip, and the excess is established. The trip record, GPS trace and fare ledger all carry trip_id TRP-00111 and the 07:47:40 start, so POL-RD-08(a) is met. On the governing distance — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern) — the trip ran 5.98 km / 24.92% over the booked 24.0 km optimal. That clears both establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not reach materiality (50% or 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile inquiry is triggered; in any event deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips, so no pattern exists.

The deviation is fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260803-014 (EV-ADVIS-00111-01) closed the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — the very segment the booked optimal route traverses — from 07:10 to 09:30, bracketing the 07:47–08:25 trip, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining after, which is the diversion the advisory itself directs. The exoneration cap is min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The justified excess is therefore the whole of the measured excess, the closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km (37.5 minutes, being 30.0 min scaled by 29.98/24.0, the amended duration being null), and nothing is left to refund on distance.

POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal, as POL-RD-03 requires:
- charged_total: SGD 37.74
- recomputed_fare: SGD 37.585 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact carrying it) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP
- refund: SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so NO_ACTION.

The rider's alternative recomputation against the booked 24.0 km optimal (giving SGD 6.74) is not the computation the clause prescribes once POL-RD-03 excuses the excess, and is not adopted. The rider's assertion that she saw no closure cites no artifact, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight, and it is contradicted by a timestamped government advisory covering the disputed segment. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route and POL-RD-02 is the operative remedy — but it produces no payable sum here. No POL-RD-05 re-quote exists (no amendment timestamps, amended_optimal_distance_km null), POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL), and POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the driver's 07:54:20 message was an announcement of the closure, the rider's only reply ('as long as i reach by 8.30') names no road and carries waypoint_hint null, so no rider-requested detour can be run. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, so there is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d of 1) does not engage the extra corroboration rule in POL-RD-08. Every artifact the ruling rests on — the trip record, the GPS trace and the traffic advisory — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so no discount applies and the confidence floor is not approached. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the charge stands and no monetary sum moves.

To both parties: I have decided this on the record. The outcome is NO_ACTION — the fare as charged stands, and the contention is settled by a capped closure exoneration rather than by any dispute about what the trace shows.

What the rider has proved. The trip identifiers and the 07:47:40 start match across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied, and on the governing figure — gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 29.98 km, not the trip record's rounded 30.0 km — the excess over the booked optimal of 24.0 km is 5.98 km, or 24.9%, clearing both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km). A deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED. The rider is also right on the subordinate points: the fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route and POL-RD-02 is the remedy clause; amended_optimal_distance_km is null and no amendment timestamp exists, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; vehicle_type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is irrelevant; and no chat message is a rider detour instruction — 'as long as i reach by 8.30' names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable.

Why the driver nevertheless succeeds. LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260803-014 (EV-ADVIS-00111-01) closes the PIE towards Tuas between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — the segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses — from 07:10 to 09:30, which brackets the whole trip and intersects the route. The trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoining on the AYE after it. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met, and the driver discharged the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him by pointing to a specific advisory and a specific clause rather than asserting bad traffic.

The cap and the arithmetic. POL-RD-03 caps the exoneration at min(measured excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. That equals the entire measured excess, so the whole of it is exonerated and no excess survives to refund. Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, with duration 30.0 x (29.98 / 24.0) = 37.5 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact carrying it) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against charged_total of 37.74. The difference of about 0.16 is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so nothing issues. The rider's claim that the 6.74 overcharge computed against the booked 24.0 km optimum should be refunded is rejected on that ground: once POL-RD-03 applies, the closure-adjusted optimum — not the booked optimum — is the correct baseline.

Remaining points. No pass-through correction arises: tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle on either party's case. No POL-RD-06 inquiry or conduct referral fires: the excess of 24.9% and 5.98 km falls below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips in 90 days. The rider's profile does not engage the extra-corroboration rule, since deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4. The driver's chat announcement at 07:54:20, read and answered by the rider without objection, is consistent with the advisory and the trace. The rider's statement that she saw no closure is a recollection citing no artifact and does not outweigh a timestamped government advisory.

Every evidence artifact in this case carries a weight_multiplier of 1.0, so no finding is discounted and no disclosure issue arises. Confidence 0.9; no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires.

ledger.claim: All three artifacts describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-00111 and the 07:47:40 start appear on the trip record, the trace and the fare ledger — so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the governing distance the trip ran 29.98 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km or 24.92%, which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%). The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence and the rider has discharged her initial burden.

The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 29.98 km, not the trip record's rounded 30.0 km; the trace figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes the threshold test run on, and it is the trace's 229 fixes at 10 second intervals with 100% coverage and no gaps that carry the excess of 5.98 km. The rider asks that the establishment test be run on that field and not on the convenience copy.

The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: no upfront quote was fixed at booking, and POL-RD-02 is therefore the operative remedy on this trip rather than a pass-through-only correction.

No exculpatory route other than the closure is open to the driver: the booked optimum of 24.0 km stands because the trip record carries no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no re-quote exists; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute a matched-itinerary baseline and solo_optimal_distance_km is irrelevant here.

The chat log records no instruction from the rider. Her only message, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', names no road and carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver: with waypoint_hint null and no road named the corroboration test cannot be run at all, and a reply fixing a time of arrival cannot be converted into a rider-requested detour that would exonerate the excess.

The driver's only route to exculpation is POL-RD-03, and that exoneration is capped: the justified excess is the lesser of the measured excess and 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00, computed from the advisory's own shortest_lawful_alternative_km on the record, and any distance beyond that cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal. The rider asks the judge to run that cap on this record's figures rather than treating the existence of the advisory as excusing the whole of the trip, and to refund whatever the cap does not cover.

On the rider's primary case, that the closure does not account for the whole of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the ruling to state charged_total, recomputed_fare and the refund on separate lines: recomputed on the booked optimum, ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = 31.00 against a charged_total of 37.74, an overcharge of 6.74; the payable figure is then rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor applies.

The rider's profile does not engage the extra corroboration rule in POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4 that the clause sets (and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, which only matters once the count reaches 4), so her claim of 24.92% excess is subject to the ordinary burden and needs no corroboration beyond the trace.

The booked optimal route runs BKE southbound then PIE westbound, and the LTA DataMall advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, from 07:10 to 09:30 on the morning of the trip. That is the exact expressway segment the optimal route traverses, it is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE, its geometry intersects the route (intersects_route true) and its validity window brackets the entire trip (overlaps_trip_window true). The first limb of POL-RD-03 is therefore satisfied on the face of the advisory, not on the driver's say-so.

The second and third limbs of POL-RD-03 are met too. The advisory directs a diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd, and the driver's route was Upper Bukit Timah then the AYE - the route leaves the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoins it further on. The trace is clean corroboration of a deliberate diversion rather than a wander: 229 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, with speeds varying by road class (0.0 / 20.6 / 46.5 / 71.0 kph) as an expressway-then-arterial-then-expressway route would. The advisory's shortest_lawful_alternative_km of 29.2 km sits almost exactly on the trace's 29.98 km.

The exoneration cap in POL-RD-03 is not reached, so the whole excess is excused. The cap is min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The justified excess is therefore the entire measured excess, the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, and no excess survives for POL-RD-02 to refund. Note the governing distance figure is the trace's 29.98 km, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires.

Even if the tribunal declined to exonerate in full, the arithmetic still lands on NO_ACTION. Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route - 29.98 km at a duration of 30.0 x (29.98 / 24.0) = 37.5 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585, against a charged_total of SGD 37.74. The difference is roughly SGD 0.16, far below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so POL-RD-02 produces NO_ACTION in any event. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

The deviation is established but is nowhere near MATERIAL. The excess of 5.98 km is 24.92% of the 24.0 km optimal: it clears the establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but falls well short of the materiality gate of 50% or 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile inquiry is not triggered at all. For completeness, were it triggered it would find nothing: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, so no pattern under POL-RD-06 exists. This is an ordinary unavoidable detour, not a material one.

The driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 places on him by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general complaint that traffic was bad. Traffic advisory ADV-20260803-014, a third-party LTA_DATAMALL closure of the very segment the optimal route uses, is invoked under POL-RD-03. That is precisely the discharge the clause demands of the driver once the rider has shown excess.

The chat log shows the diversion was announced in advance and not contested. At 07:54:20 the driver messaged the rider in-app that the PIE towards Tuas was closed by a lorry fire and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang; the rider read the message at 07:54:48 and replied at 07:54:55 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. The driver's contemporaneous account matches the LTA advisory and the trace, which is why his account of the closure should be preferred over the rider's later recollection.

There is no ERP or toll pass-through correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09. The fare breakdown carries tolls_erp of 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the optimal route crosses no gantry at this hour (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Even on the rider's best case, the standalone pass-through limb of POL-RD-09(2) has nothing to settle and adds nothing to the claim.

The rider's assertion 'I did not see any closure' cites no artifact and is contradicted by a timestamped government advisory covering the disputed segment. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded; it cannot outweigh ADV-20260803-014, which was active from 07:10 and covered the whole trip window. The rider's own profile is context only and she meets none of the gateways that would let any profile field stand in for evidence about this trip.
